title: Holiday flight
topic: A friend subtracts local takeoff and landing times on a coast-to-coast flight
blurb: A friend is packing movies for an upcoming flight.
prompt: A friend just sent this in the group chat. Tap a line if something doesn't add up, or let it pass.

segments.label: The ticket
segments.text: Booked my Christmas flight from San Francisco to Boston — leaves 8:30 AM local, lands 5:00 PM local.

segments.label: The clock
segments.text: My sister's picking me up at 5:30 Boston time (2:30 back home) so we can beat the dinner rush.

segments.label: The prep
segments.text: Eight and a half hours in a middle seat is brutal, so I'm downloading four movies tonight.

segments.label: The seat
segments.text: Throwing a power bank in my backpack so my tablet survives the flight.

conclusion: 8:30 AM to 5:00 PM is 8.5 hours in a middle seat, so I'm downloading four movies.

flaws.original: 8:30 AM in San Francisco is already 11:30 AM in Boston — landing at 5:00 PM is only 5.5 hours in the air, not 8.5.
flaws.corrupted: Eight and a half hours in a middle seat is brutal, so I'm downloading four movies tonight.

diagnosis_choices.label: 8:30 AM in SF is already 11:30 AM in Boston — you're only in the air 5.5 hours, not 8.5.
Since Boston is 3 hours ahead, add 3 hours to 8.5 — the flight is actually 11.5 hours.
8:30 AM to 5:00 PM is 9.5 hours, not 8.5, so four movies won't cover the flight.
Boarding and taxiing eat an hour of the 8.5 hours, leaving 7.5 hours for movies.

fix_choices.label: Put both clocks in Boston time (11:30 AM to 5:00 PM): 5.5 hours in the air, two movies tops.
Add the 3-hour jump for an 11.5-hour flight and download six movies instead.
Subtract an hour for taxiing so you download three movies for 7.5 hours.
Recount 8:30 AM to 5:00 PM as 9.5 hours and download a fifth movie.

flaws.explanation: 8:30 AM in San Francisco is already 11:30 AM in Boston. Those three missing hours are the time-zone jump, not flying time — it's a 5.5-hour flight.
flaws.why_tempting: 8:30 to 5:00 is instant clock subtraction, and the time-zone conversion already showed up on line 2 for dinner pickup, so your brain thinks it's handled.
flaws.catch_rule: Before subtracting departure and arrival times, put both clocks in the same time zone.
flaws.hint: When the plane lifts off at 8:30 AM in San Francisco, what time is it in Boston?

practice.problem: A flight leaves New York at 6:00 PM local and lands in Los Angeles (3 hours behind) at 9:15 PM local. How long is the flight?
practice.answer: 6 hours 15 minutes — 6:00 PM in NY is 3:00 PM in LA, and 3:00 PM to 9:15 PM is 6h 15m.

diagnosis: Airlines print both departure and arrival in departure-city time, so 5:00 PM is still San Francisco time.
8:30 AM to 5:00 PM crosses noon, so subtracting without 24-hour time drops an hour.
Local landing time already includes 45 minutes of taxiing and baggage claim at Logan.
A nonstop eastbound flight can't take off at 8:30 AM and land at 5:00 PM — there must be a hidden layover.
fix: Check if 5:00 PM on the itinerary is Pacific time instead of Boston time.
Confirm the flight doesn't include a 3-hour stopover in Chicago.
Subtract 45 minutes for baggage claim from the 5:00 PM arrival.

diagnosis: 5:30 PM Boston time is 8:30 PM San Francisco time, not 2:30 PM — you reversed the 3-hour difference.
Landing at 5:00 PM only leaves 30 minutes to get off the plane and reach pickup by 5:30.
Because of winter daylight saving time, Boston is only 2 hours ahead of San Francisco in December.
Checking in at 2:30 PM body time means you won't even be hungry for a 5:30 PM dinner.
fix: Flip the conversion: 5:30 PM Boston time is 8:30 PM back home.
Push pickup to 6:00 PM so 30 minutes at baggage claim doesn't make her circle.
Check whether the winter gap between SF and Boston is 2 hours instead of 3.
Eat a late lunch on the plane instead of planning a 5:30 dinner.

diagnosis: Four movies only run about 6 hours, so a power bank won't even be needed on an 8.5-hour flight.
Airlines ban power banks in backpacks under the seat — they have to stay in checked luggage.
A tablet lasts 10+ hours on airplane mode, so carrying a power bank for 8.5 hours is extra weight.
You'll need a wall plug for the middle seat anyway since four movies run 11.5 hours with the time jump.
fix: Skip the power bank — two movies on a 5.5-hour flight won't drain a tablet.
Put the power bank in your checked bag before TSA security.
Charge the tablet to 100% at the gate and leave the battery pack at home.
Bring a second cable in case the seatback USB port works.

clean_segments: Booked my Christmas flight from San Francisco to Boston — leaves 8:30 AM local, lands 5:00 PM local.
My sister's picking me up at 5:30 Boston time (2:30 back home) so we can beat the dinner rush.
8:30 AM in San Francisco is already 11:30 AM in Boston — landing at 5:00 PM is only 5.5 hours in the air, not 8.5.
Throwing a power bank in my backpack so my tablet survives the flight.
clean_conclusion: 8:30 AM in SF is 11:30 AM in Boston — you're only in the air 5.5 hours, not 8.5.
